newsitem.title: UK: NZ SPORT GOLF-Pressure off Turner ahead of British Open.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT GOLF-Pressure off Turner ahead of British Open.

text.p: LOCK LOMOND, Scotland, July 8 - For the first time in some years Greg Turner can spend the next fortnight not having to worry about qualifying for the British Open golf tournament, NZPA reports.

Turner, who is New Zealand's sole representative in this week's Stg800,000 ($NZ2,020,000) Loch Lomond world invitational tournament, earned an exemption into next week's Open at Royal Troon after finishing seventh in the event last year.
"I can concentrate on the job at hand because it's the first year in a while that I have had the British Open in my schedule knowing for sure that I was going to be in the championship," Turner said.
"Being exempt has taken a lot of pressure off me."
Turner comes into this week's Scottish event, set on the shoreline of Loch Lomond, fresh from a week off.

He and his wife Jane spent last week at Wimbledon courtesy of tickets given to them by close friend and New Zealand tennis No 1 Brett Steven, who made it through to the last 16 of the All England championships.

The Loch Lomond event has attracted some of the world's best players including Greg Norman, dual US Open champion Ernie Els, defending British Open champion Tom Lehman and past majors winners Larry Mize and Payne Stewart.
European Tour players chasing the Stg133,330 ($NZ337,000) British Open winner's cheque include Colin Montgomery, fresh from winning last week's Irish Open, Nick Faldo, Ian Woosnam and Darren Clarke.
"Loch Lomond is a fantastic course and it's going to be a really good test in the presence of a really strong field," Turner said.
"It's just the ideal sort of week for preparing for the British Open."
Royal Troon will be Turner's maiden appearance at the Aryeshire-located course which last staged a British Open in 1989.
"It's the only British Open venue where I haven't played so I am looking forward to it from that point of view," Turner said.
"It's important that I am exempt because it gives me the chance to play two or three more practice rounds than I would otherwise have had."
